data.body:
rebar-debug Phase 1 disposition — design escalation tracked.

Problem: the two named synchronous Pydantic-AI tests emit `DeprecationWarning: There is no current event loop`.

Reproduction/proof: `pytest "tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py::test_the_outbound_payload_is_equivalent_across_providers[frontier]" tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py::test_usage_limits_on_run_not_constructor -W error::DeprecationWarning -q` deterministically fails before the Anthropic boundary. The captured rebar failure is `model=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 ... There is no current event loop`. The dynamic call path is rebar `PydanticAIRunner.run` -> documented Pydantic AI `Agent.run_sync` -> `pydantic_ai._utils.get_event_loop` -> `asyncio.get_event_loop()` at installed pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.2 `_utils.py:1128`.

Ownership finding: latest compatible v1 (1.107.5) retains the same lookup, and current v2.31.1 also calls `asyncio.get_event_loop()`, so an ordinary dependency upgrade does not remediate it. Upstream pydantic/pydantic-ai issue #1196 is OPEN and labeled `bug`, `needs-discussion`, and `v3`: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/1196. The maintainer investigation says always creating a loop breaks persistent httpx client loop affinity (#748), while caching a loop can reuse it after default-executor shutdown; upstream therefore defers a proper held-Runner/dedicated-thread design to v3.

Classification: valid upstream dependency defect, but no proven safe rebar-owned repair. Rebar is using the dependency’s public synchronous API as intended. A rebar change must choose explicitly between (A) taking lifecycle ownership with equivalent persistent-client and executor-shutdown guarantees, or (B) narrowly suppressing the known Python 3.12/3.13 warning while leaving upstream behavior intact. Upgrading within v1 or to current v2 does not resolve it. Per the ticket plan and user instruction to batch design/not-a-bug choices, no Phase 2 code change is authorized yet.

Escalation list entry: socialized-exclusive-mouse — choose rebar-owned loop lifecycle vs exact upstream-warning suppression vs wait for upstream v3. Recommended disposition: narrow warning suppression in test configuration only if warning-clean CI is required now; otherwise accept the upstream warning until v3, because rebar-owned lifecycle duplicates a subtle dependency invariant.
